slides: Welcome back. Now two exam favorites in motion. The speed changes by a percent, and answers written with letters.

slides.say: Remember from work and rate. When the job is the same, the rate and the time go opposite ways. In motion, the route is the job. So on the same route, the speed and the time go opposite ways.
So we write the change of the speed as a fraction, and we flip it for the time.
at: and we flip it for the time

slides.say: Now a new example. On the same route, the speed is twenty-five percent faster. Twenty-five percent more is times one and a quarter, five quarters.
We flip five quarters to four fifths. So the time is times four fifths. That's one fifth less, twenty percent less time.
at: We flip five quarters to four fifths

slides.say: So a trip of sixty minutes takes sixty times four fifths, forty-eight minutes.
Careful, twenty-five percent faster does not mean twenty-five percent less time. It's only twenty percent less.
Another example. Fifty percent faster is times three halves. So the time is times two thirds.
at: Fifty percent faster is times three halves

slides.say: And slower works the same way. Twenty percent slower is times four fifths. So the time is times five quarters.
at: Twenty percent slower is times four fifths

slides.say: Five quarters means a quarter more, so twenty-five percent more time.
at: Five quarters means a quarter more

slides.say: Now let's look at letters. When the choices have letters, plugging in numbers is our safety net, like in topic fifty-one.
at: plugging in numbers is our safety net

slides.say: We pick easy numbers that the question allows. We find the answer with those numbers. That's our target. Then we put the same numbers into every choice.
If two choices give the target, we try new numbers, but only on those two.
at: If two choices give the target

slides.say: And there's a quick check with no numbers. We look at the units. If they ask for a time, the right choice must come out as a time.

slides: We'll see one question of each kind now. I'll see you in the next question.
